scores.evidence: Yjs's version summary doesn't cover deletions
scores.rationale: Correct on the subtle Yjs points (GC vs history, state vectors, no per-edit permissions inside a CRDT, fencing); only minor imprecision such as NOTIFY being lossy, which it backs up.

scores.evidence: Full offline mode ... Deferred. Bring forward when over 5% of editing sessions include a disconnect longer than 2 minutes
scores.rationale: Covers core collaborative editing with explicit, reasoned deferrals, but the eight-phase scope with no stated team size makes feasibility somewhat assumed.

scores.evidence: Each open document has exactly one owner server: it holds the doc in memory and is the only one writing it to storage.
scores.rationale: Ownership, lease/fencing, permissions, derived data and tenancy are handled consistently across phases, with intentional supersessions (write order) flagged.

scores.evidence: divergence detector in prod: idle clients send what they have plus a content hash... Crashes: 500 random kills and 3 database failovers lose 0 confirmed edits.
scores.rationale: Validation is specific to the risks, early and continues in prod, but thresholds (100k sessions, 7 nights, 500 kills) are stated without justification or provisional labels.

scores.evidence: 95% of keystrokes should reach other screens within 250 ms in the same region.
scores.rationale: Revisit triggers show what would change the design, but scale, team size and budget are never stated and many figures are presented as given.

scores.evidence: an update that breaks loading is quarantined (document flagged, on-call paged) instead of crash-looping the server
scores.rationale: Covers divergence, stale owners, DB outage, revocation misses, malicious updates and uploads, overload and duplicates, each with detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: a synthetic test runs every minute (Checkly with Playwright)... one rollback to the previous build has been done.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, canary, runbooks, paging and restore drills are concrete, though team size and the burden of Envoy, chaos tests and pen tests are not sized.

scores.evidence: Keep every snapshot and the full log for now... storage is cheap.
scores.rationale: Cost is only touched through build-vs-buy and 'use 3 servers, not 30'. There are no estimates, no scaling of connections, memory or storage with usage, and no cost model.

scores.evidence: `tenant_id` is on every row, token and log line from the first migration... Documents stay in Yjs format, so switching either way stays cheap.
scores.rationale: One-way decisions are marked 'lock it down' and validated early, with deferral, add-only schema rules, exit paths and revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Use 3 servers, not 30, and keep autoscaling simple until the data says otherwise.
scores.rationale: Starts with one process and defers many items, but the chaos tests, pen tests, WAF, Envoy and multi-phase gates add some ceremony.

scores.evidence: Build order inside Phase 0 (widest impact first): tenant/user/document ID model → `doc_updates` table → login and token handshake → WebSocket edit path → editor UI.
scores.rationale: Dependencies are justified, tasks are specific, each phase has checkable exit criteria and the revisit triggers say how to adapt.

checklist.evidence: CRDT: Yjs, pinned to an exact version... Never build our own CRDT or editor core.
ProseMirror schema v1 with a minimal set of node types, and a `schema_version` per doc. Changes only add things
Simulation harness: many simulated clients... delays, reordering, duplicates, drops, partitions, server restarts. It asserts that every copy and the stored data end up identical.
'Saved' only appears after the edit is committed in Postgres... full snapshot every 500 updates... Yjs garbage collection stays on
Each open document has exactly one owner server... Disconnect clients that fall more than 4 MB behind (they resync).
Keep a copy in the browser's IndexedDB so a crashed tab keeps unconfirmed edits... Full offline mode ... Deferred
The server owning the document re-checks open connections and closes or downgrades them within 5 s.
Undo only reverts your own edits, never a collaborator's... Restore is a new edit... never rewrites the log.
Remote cursors and selections via the y-prosemirror cursor plugin... nothing is stored and nothing depends on it
Phase 1: Lock and prove the document format... Simulation: 100k sessions a night with zero divergence, 7 nights in a row.
A document over 25 MB becomes read-only with a banner and an alert... 50 people editing one document with cursors on stays within the latency target
the protocol version is sent on connect, and the current and previous versions are both supported.

traps.evidence: Edits merge in any order, so reconnect, multiple servers and offline stay possible without a rewrite.
Never build our own CRDT or editor core.
get one keystroke working end-to-end in prod → freeze and test the document format
you can't check permissions edit by edit inside a CRDT

note: Very strong, technically sound plan that uses Yjs, builds the sync core first and proves it, and handles failure modes and reversibility well; its weak points are near-absent cost reasoning and unstated scale and team assumptions.
